rows.question: Can I resit an exam I already passed to get a higher grade?
rows.answer: No, you cannot resit an exam you have already passed to get a higher grade. For instance, in The Art of Science Communication [1], Evolutionary Computing [3], and Knowledge Organization [4], the only resit opportunities are for components you initially fail. Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning [5] does not offer resits for any assignments or essays. Therefore, once you pass an exam, you cannot attempt it again for a better grade.

rows.question: Is a final mark of 5.45 a pass?
rows.answer: No, a final mark of 5.45 is not a pass. According to the general programme rules [1], a final mark below 5.50 is rounded down, meaning a mark of 5.45 would be rounded to 5.0, which is below the passing threshold of 6.0.

rows.question: When am I allowed to start my Master Project AI?
rows.answer: You must have completed 60 ECTS in total from the MSc Artificial Intelligence program before starting the Master Project AI [1].

rows.question: How many EC is the Master Project AI?
rows.answer: The Master Project AI is worth 30 EC (30 ECTS credits) [1].

rows.question: Can I redo the Evolutionary Computing programming assignment if I fail it?
rows.answer: No, you cannot redo the programming assignment if you fail it. According to the course rules [1], there is no resit possible for the programming assignment. However, if you pass the exam and fail the programming assignment, you can keep the grade of the passed exam component for next year or later, provided you then get a good grade (> 5.5) for the missing component.

rows.question: If I pass the Evolutionary Computing exam but fail the assignment, do I lose my exam grade?
rows.answer: No, if you pass the exam but fail the programming assignment, you can keep the grade of the passed exam component for next year or later. Then, you can pass the course by getting a good grade (> 5.5) for the missing assignment component and using the old exam grade in the averaging formula [1].

rows.question: How is Deep Learning graded?
rows.answer: Deep Learning (XM_0083) is graded based on a final exam (50%) and practical assignments (50%). You must pass the final exam with a sufficient grade (equivalent to a grade of 5.5 or higher), and practical assignments cannot be redone if they do not meet the required standard. [1]

rows.question: Who coordinates the Evolutionary Computing course?
rows.answer: The Evolutionary Computing course is coordinated by prof. dr. A.E. Eiben [1].

rows.question: I already completed Advanced Machine Learning. Can I take Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning?
rows.answer: No, you cannot take Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning (XM_0189) if you have already completed Advanced Machine Learning (XM_0010) due to the transitional provisions stated in [1].

rows.question: What is the deadline to request an extra exam opportunity, and who qualifies?
rows.answer: The deadline to request an extra examination opportunity is 15 July, and it is available to students who have completed all but one unit of education to meet the requirements of the degree and have failed the examination during all previously offered attempts, unless participation in an examination was not possible for compelling reasons [1].

rows.question: How long after an exam can I inspect my graded work?
rows.answer: You have the right to inspect your graded examination within twenty working days after the results are announced, but no later than ten working days before the resit opportunity [1].

rows.question: How long does an examiner have to grade a written exam?
rows.answer: According to the general programme rules [1], an examiner has up to fifteen working days to determine the result of a written examination.

rows.question: I have a CS bachelor. Should I take Cognitive Psychology and its Applications or Skills for AI?
rows.answer: Based on the programme rules, as a student with a CS bachelor, you should choose the course Cognitive Psychology and its Applications [4]. This course contributes to the core qualifications of a graduate in the MSc Artificial Intelligence programme [1].

rows.question: Is there a resit for the group homework in Multi-Agent Systems?
rows.answer: No resit is offered for the group homework assignments in Multi-Agent Systems [1].

rows.question: If I fail AI and Society, can I do a resit?
rows.answer: No resit is possible for any component of AI and Society [1].

rows.question: How much does the final essay count for in AI and Society?
rows.answer: The final essay counts for 50% of the total grade in AI and Society [1].

rows.question: Can I retake an NLP practical assignment to improve my grade?
rows.answer: No, you cannot retake an NLP practical assignment to improve your grade. According to [1], retakes of practical assignments to improve the grade are not allowed.

rows.question: What happens if I hand in an NLP assignment a few hours late?
rows.answer: If you hand in an NLP assignment a few hours late, it will be assessed a 10% penalty [4]. However, assignments submitted up to 24 hours after the deadline will still be accepted [4].

rows.question: In which period is Natural Language Processing taught?
rows.answer: Natural Language Processing (XM_0121) is taught in period P5, as stated in source [1].

rows.question: Who coordinates Multi-Agent Systems?
rows.answer: The course coordinator for Multi-Agent Systems (XM_0052) is dr. E.J.E. Pauwels [1].

rows.question: What grade do I need on each part of Knowledge Representation?
rows.answer: You need a minimum grade of 5.5 in each component of the Knowledge Representation course, including the weekly homework, group assignments, peer reviewing assignment reports, and the written exam [1].

rows.question: I failed Experimental Design and Data Analysis. What can I retake?
rows.answer: If you failed Experimental Design and Data Analysis, you can only retake the individual digital test as part of the re-examination policy [1].

rows.question: What level is the Machine Learning for Graphs course?
rows.answer: The Machine Learning for Graphs course is a level 600 course [1].

rows.question: How is Climate Risk Assessment for the Financial Sector graded?
rows.answer: Climate Risk Assessment for the Financial Sector is graded through an individual written exam worth 70% and three group assignments, each counting for 10%, making up the remaining 30% of the grade [5].

rows.question: What do I need to pass Econometrics for Quantitative Finance?
rows.answer: To pass Econometrics for Quantitative Finance, you need a minimum final grade of 5.5, with a minimum grade of 5.0 on the written exam. If your written exam grade is 5.0 or higher, your final grade is calculated as a weighted average of the written exam and case work [1].

rows.question: Can I get an exemption from my master's thesis?
rows.answer: According to the rules outlined in [2], you may be eligible for an exemption from one or more examination components, including the master's thesis, if you have either passed a unit of education at a university or university of applied sciences (HBO) or a research university (WO) that is equivalent in terms of content and level, or have demonstrated through your work and/or professional experience that you have sufficient knowledge and skills with regard to the relevant unit of education. However, the final project, which in this case would be your master's thesis, is excluded from this exemption possibility. [2]

rows.question: How long do my passed exam results stay valid?
rows.answer: The validity period of examinations passed and exemption from examinations is unlimited, unless otherwise specified [1].

rows.question: Will there be a second examiner at my oral exam?
rows.answer: According to the programme rules [1], a second examiner is typically present during oral examinations unless the Examination Board has determined otherwise. Therefore, there will usually be a second examiner at your oral exam.

rows.question: How quickly will I get the result of an oral exam?
rows.answer: You will get the result of an oral exam as soon as possible, but at the latest within two working days after the examination has finished [1][2][3][4][5].

rows.question: I have dyslexia. What do I need to submit to get exam facilities?
rows.answer: You need to provide a statement from a BIG-, NIP-, or NVO-registered professional who is qualified to conduct a psychological evaluation, as stated in [1][3].

rows.question: What IELTS score do I need to be admitted?
rows.answer: You need an overall IELTS Academic score of at least 6.5, with a minimum score of 6.0 for each subcomponent (Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking) to meet the English language requirement for admission [1].

rows.question: How many EC is the whole AI master's programme?
rows.answer: The entire AI master's programme is worth 120 EC (120 ECTS credits) [3].

rows.question: Which specialisations can I choose in the AI master?
rows.answer: You can choose between the specialisations "Cognitive Science" and "AI for Health," or you can opt for a coherent set of electives. [1][4]

rows.question: Who decides if my situation isn't covered by the exam regulations?
rows.answer: In instances not regulated by the Teaching and Examination Regulations or in the event of demonstrable extreme unreasonableness or unfairness, the faculty board responsible for the study programme will decide, unless the matter concerned is the responsibility of the Examination Board [1].

rows.question: How soon after the first exam's results can the resit be held?
rows.answer: According to the general programme rules [2], the resit for a (partial) examination may not take place within ten working days of the announcement of the results for the original (partial) examination. This applies to the final written exam in Skills for AI [1].

rows.question: Can I take an elective that isn't on the programme's list?
rows.answer: No, you should only choose electives from the list provided by the programme. According to [1], you are required to choose 3 electives from the specified list for the Climate and Sustainable Finance programme. Taking an elective not on the list is not allowed.

rows.question: The regulations say there are two exam opportunities per year. Does that mean I can resit the AI and Society essay?
rows.answer: According to the course-specific regulations for AI and Society [1], there is no option for a resit for the individual final essay. Therefore, you cannot resit the essay even if you did not pass it initially. [1]

rows.question: I have a Computer Science bachelor with 12 EC of AI courses. Am I directly admissible?
rows.answer: Yes, you are directly admissible to the Master's programme in Artificial Intelligence if you hold a university-level Bachelor's degree in Computer Science with at least 12 ECTS in AI key area courses, according to the admission requirements [1]. However, you should consider choosing the course "Cognitive Psychology and its Application" as recommended for students with a Computer Science background [2].

rows.question: I'm in the Cognitive Science specialisation and have 48 EC. Can I start my master thesis?
rows.answer: According to the course-specific rules for the Master Thesis: Research Project Cognitive Science [1], you can start your master thesis after completing the required courses for the Cognitive Science specialisation. Since you have 48 EC, which aligns with the requirements for this specialisation, you are eligible to begin your master thesis. [1]

rows.question: My final grade for a course is 5.5. Did I pass?
rows.answer: Based on the information provided, whether you passed the course depends on the specific course. For AI for Security [1], if your weighted average is 5.5 or higher, you will receive an NVD (which is not a failing grade). However, for other courses like Econometrics for Quantitative Finance [2], you need a minimum final grade of 5.5, so a grade of 5.5 would be a pass. Therefore, you passed the AI for Security course but not necessarily other courses. [1][2]

rows.question: I've failed my last remaining course twice. Can I get a third attempt?
rows.answer: According to the general programme rules [5], if you have failed a course during all previously offered attempts, you may request an additional examination opportunity from the Examination Board, provided you have completed all but one unit of your degree and participation in the examination was not possible for compelling reasons. Requests must be submitted by 15 July.
